videos.why: A question every park visitor can feel (how many hours of costume pay is one ticket), answer held back to a 9-hours payoff on the castle clock; frame 0 shows the Disneyland logo, the castle and the $224 ticket.
strengths: Title asks and names Disneyland, no figure given away
Everyday thing (a park ticket) gone behind to the workers' pay
Pick-one ending with both ticket prices on screen
risks: salary-style topic is a lane we have not tested before

videos.why: The niche's top breakout question (what a petrol pump makes, 1.26M views) told from Rohan's tank with sourced NACS figures; frame 0 is a recognisable forecourt with the 65%-of-sales tag, and the 38.8% gross-profit payoff is held back. Ranked above AMC for the proven lane and clearer first frame; below Disneyland, whose payoff is easier to feel.
strengths: Everyday thing (filling the tank) gone behind to the business
Title and hook ask without giving the payoff
Six directed places, payoff on a roadside price sign
risks: The card fee per store is a long spoken figure
Figures are US convenience stores, told to a global audience

videos.why: Strong 'thing in your hand' mechanism (half the ticket goes to the studio, the food costs AMC 18% of the snack price), but the hook is a why-question with no figure spoken and the payoff needs the earlier beats; rank's 5.9 counts its QA retries, which are fixed.
strengths: AMC logo and the $12.73 ticket in frame 0
Clear hidden-payer story: studio takes the ticket, popcorn pays AMC
Popcorn tub fill line shows the 18% visually
risks: Owner marked a how_they_make_money Short stale before
